title: Your Task Templates Are Already Playbooks
summary: Your case management task templates already describe PI follow-up. See how Hona's AI case agent, Lia, runs them as playbooks and logs the work to the case.
body_markdown:
Open your case management software and look at the task templates for a new personal injury case. Call the client after intake. Confirm the first appointment. Check in after the visit. Request records when treatment ends. Someone at your firm wrote those steps down years ago, and they are still right.


The list is fine. Every item on it is a reminder, though, and a reminder needs a person to act on it.


## A reminder is not a follow-up


Case management software is good at recording the work. It can tell a case manager to call a client. It cannot make the call, notice that the client stopped answering, or try again on Thursday.


That gap matters most in pre-litigation. In an Insurance Research Council study of auto injury claims published in July 2026, about 4 in 5 claimants resolved their claims without a lawsuit, and represented claims took a median of about 440 days. That is more than a year of appointments, check-ins and records requests on every case your firm carries.


## What happens when the reminder sits


When one case manager carries 100 or more active cases, reminders pile up. The cost shows up in predictable places:


- **A missed appointment** turns into a gap in treatment.
- **A gap in treatment** becomes the insurer's argument that the injury was minor.
- **A provider office that never answered** leaves the demand waiting on bills.
- **A client who heard nothing for six weeks** starts calling other firms.


None of this happens because your team does not know what to do. It happens because the task list is longer than the day.


## Turn the template into a playbook


A Hona playbook is the same procedure, written so Lia, Hona's AI case agent, can run it. Each one has three parts: when it starts, what Lia does, and when it stops. Escalation rules sit inside it in plain language, the way you would explain them to a new hire.


So "confirm the first appointment" stops being a line on someone's list. Lia texts and emails the client a reminder, follows up after the visit to confirm they went, and picks up any new provider they mention. If the client misses the visit and cannot be reached, she escalates to your team with the reason, what she already tried and a priority.


Hona ships standard playbooks for care coordination, provider follow-up and escalations. Hona's forward-deployed team builds custom playbooks with your firm for the procedures that make your firm different. Your team can read any playbook and change it in plain language.


## Your case management software stays put


None of this asks you to switch systems. Your case management software stays the record of the case. Hona reads cases and phases from it, does the follow-up, and writes the results back. Texts, Lia's included, are logged to the case. Notification history lands as notes, client files arrive as attachments, and form answers can update case fields.


The guide walks through all ten stages of pre-litigation, from intake to close-out. For each one, it shows what your software already handles and what Hona takes on. It also covers how your team stays in control: what Lia escalates, what she never answers, and when she sends messages.


[Read the guide: Personal injury pre-litigation with your case management software](https://www.hona.com/guides/pre-litigation-case-management-software)


## The takeaway


Your firm already wrote its playbooks. They are sitting in your task templates as reminders. Hona turns them into work that gets done, and logs that work back to the case your team already uses.
